div.head: Af 17
div.ab: Gif hwa oðrum his unmagan oðfæste, ⁊ he hine on þære fæstinge forforie, getreowsie hine facnes se ðe hine fede, gif hine hwa hwylces teo.
Gif hwa oðrum his unmagan oðfæste, ⁊ he hine on ðære fæstinge forferie, getriowe hine facnes se ðe hine fede, gif hine hwa hwelces teo.
Si quis alii suum quid imbecille commendet, et in illa commendatione moriatur, adlegiet se facinoris qui pascebat illud, si ab aliquo compellatur inde.
Gif hwa oðrum his unmagan oðfæste, ⁊ he hine on ðære fæstinge forferie, getriowe hine facnes se ðe hine fede, gif hine hwa hwelces teo.

If someone entrusts his dependent [child] to another, and [the guardian] allows it to die while in that care, let [the guardian] who supported him clear himself of wrongdoing, if someone accuses him of something.

If anyone entrusts a [child or other] helpless person who is dependent on him to another, and the person accepting the charge causes the death of the person committed to him, he who nurtured him shall clear himself of criminal intention, if anyone prefers such an accusation against him.
If anyone entrusts to another one of his helpless dependants, and he dies during that time of fostering, he who reared him is to clear himself of guilt, if anyone accuses him of any.

Wenn einer einem anderen seinen Unmündigen anvertraut, und dieser in der Pflegehut stirbt, so schwöre sich der, welcher diesen verpflegt, von der Verschuldung rein, falls ihn jemand irgend welcher bezichtigt.
If someone entrusts his minor child to another, and the child dies in that fostering, let the one who fed him clear himself by oath of wrongdoing, if anyone accuses him of any.

note.label: cf.
note.quote: MP §28 discusses the responsibility of a person who has had any property entrusted to him; he must likewise swear his innocence

div.note: So Liebermann, but the dictionaries and Attenborough take the expression hine forferie, which seems unique, to mean “cause or allow to die”, and the subject would then be the guardian.
